source: FAO Regional Office for Asia and the Pacific, Swine Health Management, Volume 2: Guide to Prevent and Control Porcine Reproductive and Respiratory Syndrome (RAP Publication 2012/27, Bangkok, 2012)
text: In litters affected by PRRS, common signs include mummified piglets (died in the womb, dry and dark brown), stillborn piglets, and weak piglets that die shortly after birth from secondary bacterial infections because their immune systems are compromised. Pre-weaning deaths can reach up to 33 percent of a litter. Piglets may be born with swollen eyelids, a sticky brown material over the eyelids, splayed legs, diarrhea, pneumonia, and coughing. Many are too weak to suckle. Over time, as the outbreak passes, more piglets survive and health improves.
